articles.title: I built a tray app to see where my Claude Code tokens actually go
articles.excerpt: You're deep in a refactor with Claude Code, everything is flowing, and then: You've hit your limit. Resets at 3:10 PM. Two hours of nothing. And the worst part isn't the wait — it's that I had no idea…
articles.body: You're deep in a refactor with Claude Code, everything is flowing, and then: You've hit your limit. Resets at 3:10 PM. Two hours of nothing. And the worst part isn't the wait — it's that I had no idea what burned the quota . Was it that one giant conversation? The 20 skills I installed "just in case"? A turn that re-read half the repo? So I built Bumeter : a small desktop app that reads the logs Claude Code and Kiro already write on your machine and answers two questions: Where did my tokens go? Per conversation, per turn, per skill. How close am I to being blocked? Your 5-hour and 7-day quota (and Kiro's monthly credits), always visible in the system tray. It's free, open source (GPL-3.0), and nothing is uploaded — it only reads files that are already on your disk.

articles.title: Parakeet that knows what a makolet is: an English-Hebrew code-switching fine-tune
articles.excerpt: I live in Jerusalem and speak English, so I talk like this all day: "I have to go to Bituach Leumi tomorrow." "Can you grab some bamba from the makolet?" "We're doing Motzei Shabbat at my savta's." Th…
articles.body: I live in Jerusalem and speak English, so I talk like this all day: "I have to go to Bituach Leumi tomorrow." "Can you grab some bamba from the makolet?" "We're doing Motzei Shabbat at my savta's." The sentences are English, but a few of the words are Hebrew, and nobody uses an English word in their place. This is code-switching , and speech recognition handles it badly. Today I'm releasing Parakeet-TDT-0.6B-v2-English-Hebrew-Codeswitching , a fine-tune of NVIDIA's parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2 that writes those Hebrew words correctly, in Latin letters. It comes as .nemo , GGUF, ONNX and sherpa-onnx, and it runs offline on an Android phone. Transcript Stock Parakeet v2 I want to go to the Micollette today to buy my groceries. This fine-tune I want to go to the makolet today to buy my groceries.

articles.body: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have unraveled some of the atmospheric secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot world that has the consistency of marshmallow. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , under the watchful infrared eye of the JWST , is WASP-17b, located around 1,300 light-years away. The exoplanet has a mass around 0.8 times that of Jupiter, but it is around twice as wide as the solar system's largest planet, giving it a "super-puff" consistency comparable to the Earth-based treat. WASP-17 b is so close to its parent star that it completes an orbit in under four Earth days, with this proximity also making the temperature of this " hot Jupiter " skyrocket.

articles.body: I am a LegalTech Attorney leading a developer team from Costa Rica. articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 16, 1975: NASA launches the 1st-ever GOES weather satellite to watch Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 16, 1975, NASA launched the first operational GOES weather satellite. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 16, 1975, NASA launched the first operational GOES satellite! GOES-A was the first in a series of weather satellites that NASA jointly operated with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). The name is short for Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite . GOES-A launched on a Delta rocket from Cape Canaveral, Florida. GOES satellites all have a geostationary orbit, which means they always face the same part of Earth — in this case, the Indian Ocean. Once GOES-A became operational, it was renamed GOES-1. The GOES satellite fleet has grown over the years, and is a critical link in the chain of satellites tracking Earth's weather from space.

For Edgerton and Connelly, "Dark Matter" has been a whirlwind project as their characters search for a safe alternate universe while being pursued by a multiplicity of Jasons. The physical rigors and emotional toll of shooting the show and presenting its nuanced storytelling often proved difficult. "There's two exhaustions that I’ve found in movie work," Edgerton tells Space.
